title: gcloud Basics: Accounts, Projects, and Configurations
intro: In Google Cloud, the project is the unit of billing, access, and resource isolation (like an AWS account or Azure subscription), grouped under folders and an organisation. gcloud 'configurations' bundle an account, project, and default region, so switching environments is one command instead of three.

steps.prompt: Show the active gcloud configuration: account, project, and defaults.
steps.fake_output:
[compute]
region = europe-west1
zone = europe-west1-b
[core]
account = alice@example.com
project = shop-dev-381204

Your active configuration is: [dev]
steps.explanation: You're alice, in the project shop-dev-381204, using the 'dev' configuration.
steps.why: Project IDs are globally unique and permanent, and often carry a numeric suffix. Always check the project before acting: it's GCP's version of 'which account am I in?'.

steps.fake_output:
NAME  IS_ACTIVE  ACCOUNT            PROJECT            COMPUTE_DEFAULT_ZONE
dev   True       alice@example.com  shop-dev-381204    europe-west1-b
prod  False      alice@example.com  shop-prod-217733   europe-west1-b
steps.why: Configurations beat running 'gcloud config set project' back and forth: each environment keeps its own account, project, and zone, so you can't half-switch (new project, old zone). You can also select one for a single command with --configuration=prod.

steps.explanation: All gcloud commands now target shop-prod-217733.
steps.why: Like 'az account set', this is global for your user and affects every terminal. In scripts, pass --project explicitly instead of relying on whatever configuration someone left active.

steps.prompt: List the APIs enabled in the current project.
steps.fake_output:
NAME                                 TITLE
compute.googleapis.com               Compute Engine API
container.googleapis.com             Kubernetes Engine API
logging.googleapis.com               Cloud Logging API
storage.googleapis.com               Cloud Storage API
steps.explanation: Four APIs are enabled. Anything else (Cloud SQL, Secret Manager...) must be enabled before use.
steps.why: GCP services are off per project until enabled, which is a common first error ('SERVICE_DISABLED'; see gcp-incident-003). Enabling APIs belongs in Terraform (google_project_service), so a new environment doesn't fail on its first deploy.

steps.prompt: Set up Application Default Credentials, so local code and tools like Terraform can authenticate as you.
steps.fake_output:
Credentials saved to file: [/home/alice/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json]
These credentials will be used by any library that requests Application Default Credentials (ADC).
steps.explanation: SDKs and Terraform on this machine now pick up your identity automatically.
steps.why: gcloud's own login and ADC are separate: 'gcloud auth login' is for the CLI, 'application-default login' is for code. Confusing the two causes endless 'could not find default credentials' errors. In production, code uses the attached service account or Workload Identity instead, never a key file.
